claim: The sprite collision flag (port 0x303B bit 0) is exact to the dot: an opaque dot written where another sprite already wrote one. Dots outside the clip window, hidden overlaps and sprites switched off by NextREG 0x15 bit 0 still collide.
limit: Measured on a KS1 (core 3.03.00, nxsuite SP01). The flag says only that some collision happened since the last read, not which sprites; a sprite the engine dropped from a line collides with nothing.

evidence.source: I. Novak, Unraveling the ZX Spectrum Next, Vol 1 (2026; core 3.03.03), chapter 16
evidence.text: The check is made in the sprite line buffer, so it follows the buffer and not the screen: transparent dots are never written and sprites side by side do not collide; reading the port clears the flag.
KS1 Issue 2, core 3.03.00 (nxsuite SP01): overlapping opaque dots collided, side by side did not; dots outside the clip window and sprites off by $15 bit 0 still collided; a read cleared the flag.
